open_points.subject: capture_failure_and_repair_slot ownership
open_points.text: “module:runs owns the conditions of capture, copying the spooled inputs” contradicts “module:functions ... only then copies each spooled file into the content-addressed area” and State 3’s “functions copies those files’ bytes after its checks”.
open_points.question: Which module owns and performs the durable copy of captured spooled files: runs or functions?
options: runs validates and copies before calling functions
runs validates, then functions validates and copies
open_points.default_guess: runs validates eligibility; functions performs the copy only after all case checks pass.

open_points.subject: pre-send instance-check order
open_points.text: A09 rule 6 orders “plain http not allowed ... a required header repeated, a required header invalid”, while State 3 says prepare_request checks “a repeated required header, a plain http target not allowed” and omits the invalid-header check from that sequence.
open_points.question: What exact order must service_invoker use for plain-HTTP, repeated-header and invalid-header pre-send failures?
options: A09 order: plain HTTP, repeated header, invalid header
State 3 order: repeated header, plain HTTP, with invalid header placed separately
open_points.default_guess: Use A09 rule 6’s explicit order: plain HTTP, repeated header, invalid header.

open_points.subject: startup recovery of unfinished runs
open_points.text: A14 rule 5 requires deriving every run that has not ended — “running, awaiting_approval or pending” — before advancing those left running, but State 4 says recover_running_runs “advances every run left running” and does not state that awaiting_approval and pending runs are first re-derived.
open_points.question: Must startup recovery re-derive every unfinished run, including stored pending and awaiting_approval runs, before selecting runs to advance?
options: Re-derive all unfinished runs, then advance those derived as running
Only inspect and advance runs whose stored status is running
open_points.default_guess: Re-derive all unfinished runs first, then advance every run whose derived status is running.

open_points.subject: materializing trial-case inputs for sandbox execution
open_points.text: “Each case ... is one call of capability:sandbox.execute_function with the implementation’s code, the case’s inputs and the contract’s bounds” does not say who turns TrialCase StoredValue and file-fixture references into the JSON values and bytes required by the sandbox.
open_points.question: Which module reads the StoredValue and fixture bytes, and through which capability, before a trial or admission execution?
options: functions calls store.read_value_bytes and passes materialized inputs to sandbox
sandbox receives references and reads their bytes
open_points.default_guess: functions calls store.read_value_bytes and passes materialized values and file bytes to sandbox.

open_points.subject: materializing operation inputs and approval previews
open_points.text: The read-only path says prepare_request “places the inputs” without naming any byte-reading step, while the effectful path says “file inputs are read through capability:store.read_value_bytes” without naming which module performs that call; value inputs stored by reference are not addressed either.
open_points.question: Which module materializes StoredValue and SpooledFile inputs before service_invoker builds the request and effects builds the approval preview?
options: effects reads all input bytes through store.read_value_bytes and passes materialized inputs to service_invoker
runs materializes inputs before calling effects
service_invoker reads store records directly
open_points.default_guess: effects reads all referenced values and files through store.read_value_bytes and passes materialized inputs to service_invoker.

open_points.subject: standing-grant effect-class lookup
open_points.text: “grant_standing_approval ... grants a node ... whose class is not destructive” names flows.read_flow_version but does not name the read needed to obtain the operation node’s binding and effect_class; FlowNode itself contains only binding_id.
open_points.question: How does effects obtain the pinned binding’s effect_class when validating a grant request?
options: effects calls bindings.read_binding for the node’s binding_id
flows returns the resolved effect_class with the node
effects re-reads the manifest operation
open_points.default_guess: effects calls bindings.read_binding and uses the accepted binding’s pinned effect_class.

open_points.subject: runs reading operation execution state
open_points.text: State 3 says runs reads “an operation element’s conclusion ... through effects.operation_element_conclusion” and never decides from another module’s raw records, but State 4 says readiness is “derived from the run’s records read through capability:store.read_records”.
open_points.question: May runs inspect raw operation NodeExecution and EffectAttempt records when deriving readiness and run answers, or must all operation state cross through effects.operation_element_conclusion?
options: All operation conclusions and output references come through effects.operation_element_conclusion
runs may read raw operation records from store
Split responsibility by naming exactly which raw fields runs may read
open_points.default_guess: Have effects.operation_element_conclusion return the conclusion and output references runs needs; runs should not re-derive operation state from raw records.

open_points.subject: timestamps in binding, flow, effect and continuation flows
open_points.text: State 4 says “a flow references the clock where a step stamps a time it names”, but propose_and_accept_binding and compose_prove_activate_flow do not reference module:clock despite writing timestamped M11, M12, M13 and M18 records; run_effect_with_approval names clock only for the transport deadline despite writing M23–M26 records; wait_resume_resolve_cancel and capture_failure_and_repair_slot omit it while recording resumptions, cancellation, capture, release and rollback times.
open_points.question: Which module calls clock.kernel_now for each timestamped write in these flows, and at what point in the corresponding store change is the timestamp obtained?
options: Each record-owning module calls clock.kernel_now immediately before its atomic store change
surface supplies one request timestamp to every called module
store timestamps records internally
open_points.default_guess: Each record-owning module calls clock.kernel_now immediately before the store change that records its action.
